title: Asked by parda-2d: Adopt the hot-path forest prototyped in parda-2d (Forest, Flat, Column) as a sylva module
body:
Adopt the hot-path forest prototyped in parda-2d (Forest, Flat, Column) as a sylva module (graft:01a10a64-df76..452c, from parda-2d)

What was needed:
- parda-2d: Move parda-2d's crates/sylva-forest (github.com/vaibhav-gopal/parda2D at 7912896; written against sylva 9d2a15d) into sylva as a module beside tree and graph, then publish. What it is: (1) Forest: ids are (slot index, generation), removing bumps the generation so stale ids fail safely, freed slots are reused; intrusive links per node (parent, first/last child, prev/next sibling, one 20-byte record per node) for O(1) push, insert-before, move and detach and O(subtree) remove with a callback per removed node; stackless preorder, postorder, children, ancestors and a skipping walk; sylva::Error for failures; to_tree exports to sylva::tree::Tree. (2) Flat: a preorder index (every slot in preorder, where each subtree ends) plus contiguous child lists, rebuilt O(n) without allocating only when Forest::version changed; full passes read the preorder array, skipping walks read the child lists with a reusable stack. (3) Column<T>: per-node data by slot, structure-of-arrays. Measured on 10k/100k-node trees (16 children per node) against a hand-written arena with a child Vec per node: full preorder 0.66/6.5 us vs 9.1/103 us (about 14x faster); dirty walk with 1% dirty 1.6/16.3 us vs 1.64/17.1 us (equal or faster); build 135-146 us/1.13 ms vs 65-78 us/1.02-1.07 ms (about 10% slower at 100k, the one gap: worth a look); Flat rebuild 42/422 us; sylva's Tree builds about 10x slower than either. Also needed for parda to publish: uuid optional (or not on this module's path), no_std + alloc friendly if cheap, wasm-compatible, published to crates.io under the library combination.

Answer (done): All of it, published: sylva 0.1.0 is on crates.io (tag v0.1.0), under the library combo (GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Royalty-Free-1.0 OR LicenseRef-Commercial-1.0; LICENSE.md adds the open-project exception to the GPL option), and github.com/vaibhav-gopal/sylva is public. Depend on it as `sylva = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }` in place of the git dependency: sylva::forest (Forest, Flat, Column, mark_with_ancestors), no uuid or serde on its path, no_std + alloc, wasm32 checked in CI. Since your prototype: the forest's accessors are #[inline] (build level with your arena at 10k, ~10% faster at 100k, measured alone), Flat::update is 1.3-1.7x faster, and reordering children takes ~9 ns at any list length. Forest is done; an incremental Flat::update remains an open todo here, for when rebuilds show up in a frame budget.
